subject: learning/forgejo-capability-bindings-and-credential-isolation
statement: Pyxis selects task tracking, code hosting, source releases, distribution releases, and artifact downloads through explicit capability bindings; each connection keeps its own provider, server, repository, and credential reference. CI mode selects native hosted checks, local verification, or both for the selected code host.
intent: Allow Forgejo and GitHub to coexist without a task operation, release download, or Git command silently using another capability's repository or account.
rationale: A single global GitHub credential and owner/name coordinate cannot distinguish identical repositories on different servers or different accounts used by task, code, and release roles. Credentials therefore remain environment references, repository-scoped Git helpers match only their bound host/path, actor caches invalidate when the bound token changes, and supervisor-captured secret names stay denied to model and verification children even if those children edit their own config.
fit_criterion: Independent-provider configuration matrices round-trip without secrets; malformed/unknown capability settings fail closed; Git helpers refuse another host or repository and restore previous settings after partial failure; verification cannot opt into a configured host token.

provenance.note: Retarget Forgejo transport onto adapters/common/forgejo after the medium-to-port move.
